title: Collective thermalization, work reliability, and resource bounds in a population-inverted Dicke Otto engine
summary: Population inversion and collective relaxation can both enhance the performance of a quantum heat engine, but through distinct mechanisms. We study a quantum Otto engine whose working medium is a symmetric collective spin of $N$ two-level constituents. For commuting work strokes and collective reservoir coupling, the dynamics reduces exactly to a finite birth--death process on the Dicke ladder, allowing a unified treatment of stationary operation, work fluctuations, and finite-time relaxation.
